blogs.title: DPO Explained: How Your Language Model Becomes Its Own Reward Model
blogs.description: A reader-friendly explainer of Direct Preference Optimization (DPO). Covers the intuition behind the reparameterization that maps reward functions to policies, why the partition function cancels under Bradley–Terry, and why this lets you skip reward fitting and RL. Suitable for ML students and engineers who want a conceptual understanding without heavy math.

blogs.title: Implementing DPO End-to-End: A Practical Tutorial for ML Practitioners
blogs.description: Step-by-step guide to implementing DPO on a modest language model (code snippets, data format, and training loop pseudocode). Includes tips on initializing the reference policy, setting beta, batching preference pairs, and validating with automatic evaluators. Ideal for engineers who want to try DPO on their own datasets.

blogs.title: DPO vs RLHF (PPO): When to Use Which and Why
blogs.description: A comparative post that breaks down strengths, weaknesses, compute and stability tradeoffs between DPO and standard RLHF using PPO. Uses intuitive examples (sentiment control, summarization, dialogue) from the paper to explain cases where DPO dominates and where PPO might still be useful. Targeted at tech leads and researchers choosing an alignment pipeline.

blogs.title: Hyperparameters, Failure Modes, and Debugging DPO
blogs.description: A practical troubleshooting guide: how to tune beta and learning rate, detect model degeneration, prevent reward-overoptimization, and diagnose distribution shift when reference or preference data differ from deployment prompts. Includes common pitfalls discovered in experiments and actionable fixes for practitioners.

blogs.title: From Human Labels to Better Chatbots: Collecting and Using Preference Data for DPO
blogs.description: Advice on designing preference-labeling workflows that work well with DPO: prompt engineering for pairwise sampling, interfaces for human raters, quality-control, and guidance on when synthetic or model-generated preferences are OK. Useful for product managers and ML ops engineers who run annotation pipelines.

blogs.title: Scaling DPO: What Changes When You Move from 6B to 70B+ Models
blogs.description: Explores engineering and research questions around applying DPO to very large models: computational cost, memory optimizations, distributed training considerations, and potential changes in generalization behavior. Aimed at ML engineers and researchers planning to scale alignment experiments.

blogs.title: DPO Beyond Text: Adapting Direct Preference Optimization to Images, Audio, and Code
blogs.description: A forward-looking post that outlines how the DPO reparameterization could be adapted for other generative modalities (image generation, speech, code synthesis) and the unique challenges each modality presents (action spaces, reference models, and evaluation). Great for multimodal researchers and enthusiasts.

blogs.title: Interpreting the Implicit Reward: Visualizing What Your DPO Model Values
blogs.description: Hands-on techniques to probe and visualize the implicit reward r_hat(x,y)=beta*log(pi_theta/pi_ref) learned by a DPO model: saliency for tokens, ranking examples by implicit reward, and case studies showing how the model's implicit values evolve during training. Intended for researchers and curious practitioners who want interpretability tools.

blogs.title: Deploying DPO-Aligned Models Safely: Monitoring, Guardrails, and Ongoing Feedback
blogs.description: A practical playbook for putting DPO-finetuned models into production: runtime evaluation metrics, human-in-the-loop monitoring for drift, safe-failure strategies, and how to use ongoing human preferences to iteratively re-train with DPO. Geared toward ML product owners and safety engineers.

blogs.title: Reproducible Experiments with DPO: Datasets, Benchmarks, and Open-Source Recipes
blogs.description: A curated resource guide that lists public preference datasets, evaluation prompts, and reproducible training recipes (with pointers to popular frameworks). Also suggests benchmark tasks and metrics to fairly compare DPO with RLHF and supervised methods. Useful for students, researchers, and open-source contributors.
